description: A `type` alias covers only its type expression; the words after it are a second token run on the line after a complete statement, so the alias owes a `;`: E-STMT-MISSING-SEMICOLON after `number` and after `"b"` (§7.2.2 rule 7), never silently dropped.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S478 "⭐ RULED — open owner questions, PA recs adopted wholesale" item 2 (g-boot-body-top-trailing-tokens-vs-semicolon-s478) — re-pinned from E-UNQUOTED-DISPLAY-TEXT ×2
rationale: §7.2.2 (S469) governs, superseding §40.8's S441 round-5 line reading ("The tokens after the end, on the statement's own line, are `E-UNQUOTED-DISPLAY-TEXT`"): a line break is whitespace (rule 4), and a second token run after a complete statement is E-STMT-MISSING-SEMICOLON after the first (rule 7). The bytes are still covered by an error, so §40.8's coverage invariant holds. The follow-on parse errors on `extra` / `more words` are a separate cascade, not asserted.
